title: Field HR Product Architect
description:
**About Sol**
-------------

Sol is an agentic HR system built for how work is changing. We're replacing the traditional HRIS with an AI-native foundation. We are built for change, designed to scale, and reimagined with AI from the ground up, so HR leaders get a clear view of their workforce instead of a system everyone works around.

At Sol, we're guided by three things: **people:** we hire driven, humble people and build to amplify their potential and our customers'; **imagination:** we challenge assumptions about our industry and how software gets built, then move fast once we've decided; and **durability:** we sweat the details to build a company that is meant to last. Day to day, that shows up as a bias toward writing things down over meetings, async communication by default, and flexible hours that respect how differently everyone works. We try new things, kill what isn't working, and hold a high bar without the politics or ego that slow good decisions down.

Sol was founded by leaders who spent decades building the modern HR category, and is backed by Sutter Hill Ventures and NEA. Our first customers go live in early 2027 and we need you to make them wildly successful.

**THE ROLE**
------------

Implementing an HRIS today means months of workshops, spreadsheets, hand-built configuration, and testing, and most of what the company learned about itself leaves with the project team. Sol is built to change that. Our agent learns what a company is trying to achieve, guides it through the right questions, and infers what it can from existing systems and documents. People confirm and verify instead of handcrafting every setting, and the system keeps learning long after go-live.

You'll lead our first customer go-lives, starting in early 2027. Your job is to make each customer successful: live on schedule, and working differently because you were there. You'll drive the implementation process and design, paired with a Forward Deployed Engineer on data migration and integrations, and advise customers on best practices and what a new HR operating model looks like when the system does more of the work.

You're also an extension of the product team. You'll be one of Sol's first users, an expert on what it can do, and the person who brings what you learn from every customer back to product and engineering. What you learn also teaches Sol's agent: you'll shape what it asks, what it recommends, and which decisions it makes on its own.

The role is a mix of strategy consulting, project management, hands-on configuration, product management, and product acceptance testing. You may know this kind of role as forward deployed, deployment strategist, or implementation lead.

This role is hybrid: onsite 3 days in San Mateo to start and then San Francisco (we move next summer).

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**
------------------

* **Scope each engagement.** Starting in pre-sales, assess fit and go-live readiness honestly, and decide what's in the first wave, what follows, and what the customer drives themselves.
* **Keep go-lives fast.** Getting customers live in a fraction of the time other systems take is core to Sol's value. Run the plan, chase decisions, clear blockers, and escalate early when something threatens the date.
* **Guide process design.** Learn how work moves through the company today, including the steps outside any system, and decide the best form for each piece in Sol: configuration, a workflow, context for the agent, or left as is for now. Some customers need a light touch; others need an opinionated perspective.
* **Lead change management.** Align stakeholders across HR, Finance, Legal, and IT. Run exec comms, a steering cadence, UAT, and sign-off discipline so decisions stick.
* **Shape the product.** Work with product and engineering regularly on what you're seeing in the field, and help decide what we build and automate next.
* **Teach the agent.** Review what Sol's agent learns from each engagement, and help decide when it's ready to make a call on its own.
* **Test before customers do.** Use new capability as it's built, and validate it against what our customers need.
* **Hand off cleanly.** Partner with your FDE through testing, cutover, and hypercare, then roll off once the customer is stable and running on their own.

**WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR**
--------------------------

* Mid-to-senior HR Operations or HRIS experience, including leading HRIS implementations more than once. Ideally Workday or comparable (Dayforce, UKG, Oracle) at companies of 1,000+ employees.
* You've lived with the system after go-live, and you know which design decisions hold up through the next comp cycle or audit. An HR Ops background is preferred; consultants who led design are welcome too.
* You understand how org structure, jobs and positions, compensation, time and leave, and payroll and benefits data depend on each other.
* You're comfortable telling a stakeholder no on scope, and you can keep a project on time without losing the room.
* You write clearly, and you can turn messy implementation reality into something product and engineering can act on.
* You're excited about what AI does to this work, including the parts of your own job it will take over.
* You're high agency and comfortable building the playbook as you go.
* **Bonus:** you've built a job architecture from scratch, or worked at a high-growth tech company or early-stage startup.

**WHY NOW**
-----------

We're early. Our first customers go live in early 2027, and how those go-lives run will set the model for every customer after them. This is the chance to fix the implementation you always wished you'd had, from the vendor side, with the product team listening. Real ownership from the first week, and a short path to a decision when you need one.

**COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS**
-----------------------------

* Base range: $200,000-$250,000 and significant early-stage equity
* Medical, dental and vision coverage
* Mental health support (Talkspace), fertility care (Kindbody) and primary care access (Teladoc, One Medical)
* FSA and dependent care accounts
* Life and disability insurance
* 401(k)
* Untracked PTO and company holidays

Sol is an equal opportunity employer. We don't discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. We're committed to building an inclusive workplace and providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities.

Job Description:

The Forward Deployment Engineer, Reporting Pro helps customers adopt DeepHealth’s Reporting Pro correctly. The role combines radiology reporting depth, clinical workflow knowledge and customer communication to design how Reporting Pro is configured for each customer, build report templates and structured reporting content with radiologists, coach implementation teams, resolve complex technical issues, and turn recurring field needs into standard product workflows, including AI-assisted report drafting as it is released.

This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports, reporting to the Service Engineering Lead, Enterprise Intelligence, and working closely with the DxS lead Forward Deployment Engineer. It operates within DeepHealth’s Forward Deployment Engineering (FDE) function, whose purpose is to help customers adopt DeepHealth products correctly. The role sits at the intersection of the Technical Delivery Manager (TDM), Product, Service and Solution Delivery teams to ensure smooth customer adoption. It transitions best practices to the Service and Solution Delivery teams and plans upcoming product changes with them to ensure commercial readiness.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* Own technical solution design and configuration of Reporting Pro for assigned customers, mapping reporting workflow to configuration (report templates, macros, structured reporting, speech recognition, sign-off and addendum rules, critical results, user roles).
* Lead technical discovery with customers and implementation teams, covering reporting workflow, legacy reporting systems, HL7 order and result flows, report distribution to RIS and EHR, network and security requirements.
* Build and validate report templates and structured reporting content with radiologists, and plan migration of templates and macros from legacy reporting systems through cutover.
* Partner with the assigned implementation counterpart for this workstream to adopt learnings and best practices into customer configuration and implementations; train and coach implementation teams and customer reporting administrators on correct configuration; publish configuration standards, template libraries and deployment playbooks.
* Serve as customer-facing technical lead during go-lives, hypercare and escalations, communicating status, options and expectations to clinical and IT stakeholders.
* Provide implementation support as the L3 escalation point for Reporting Pro issues in assigned accounts, including report delivery failures, root cause analysis and resolution with engineering (approximately 20–30% of time).
* Convert recurring customer needs into standardized workflows and product requirements, distinguishing product gaps from configuration or training issues.
* Own escalation of engineering issues for assigned accounts: triage, document reproducible defects, track status with engineering and close the loop with customers.
* Support site reliability (SRE) for assigned accounts: monitor service health with observability tools, participate in incident response and drive reliability improvements with engineering.
* Own the AI adoption strategy for Reporting Pro: define requirements, expected customer impact and success criteria, and feed them back to Product and Engineering.
* Configure, deploy and support customer adoption of AI-enabled reporting workflows (e.g., AI report drafting using priors and clinical data) as they are released, coordinating rollout, site readiness and customer adoption with the Technical Delivery Manager and Product Manager.
* Validate releases and hotfixes against representative customer configurations before and after deployment.

PLEASE NOTE: This is not an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities and requirements of the position described above. Other functions may be assigned and management retains the right to add or change duties at any time.

**Job requirements**
--------------------

**Minimum Qualifications, Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering, Health Informatics, Information Systems or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience (required).
* 8+ years of overall experience in healthcare IT, medical imaging or clinical systems (required).
* 5+ years in a customer-facing technical role for radiology reporting systems (e.g., PowerScribe, Fluency or similar), such as reporting system administrator, applications/technical consultant, implementation engineer or L3 engineer (required).
* Working knowledge of HL7 v2 (ADT, ORM, ORU), including how orders link to reports and how signed reports, addenda and corrections are distributed to RIS and EHR (required).
* Hands-on configuration of report templates, macros, structured reporting and speech recognition, including at least one reporting system go-live or migration (required).
* Strong understanding of radiology clinical workflow, including RIS, worklists, reading, dictation, sign-off and critical results communication (required).
* Working knowledge of cloud-hosted applications (GCP, AWS or Azure), storage, networking and SSO/authentication (required).
* Demonstrated ability to communicate technical decisions to radiologists, IT leaders and executives, including in escalated situations (required).
* Imaging informatics or clinical credential such as CIIP, PARCA or ARRT(R) (preferred).
* Experience with AI-assisted or LLM-based report generation in radiology, and working knowledge of DICOM and PACS integration (preferred).
* Experience in a regulated medical device environment (FDA 21 CFR 820, ISO 13485, IEC 62304).
* Microsoft Office experience required.

**Quality Standards**

* Communicates, cooperates, and consistently functions professionally and harmoniously with all levels of supervision, co-workers, visitors, and vendors.
* Demonstrates initiative, personal awareness, professionalism and integrity, and exercises confidentiality in all areas of performance.
* Follows all local, regional and country laws concerning employment.
* Follows all DeepHealth policies and procedures.
* Follows data privacy, compliance, safety and confidentiality standards at all times.
* Practices universal safety precautions.
* Promotes good public relations on the phone and in person.
* Adapts and is willing to learn new tasks, methods, and systems.
* Reports to work regularly as scheduled; consistently punctual with respect to working hours, meal and rest breaks, and maintains satisfactory personal attendance in accordance with DeepHealth guidelines.

**Travel**

This position requires domestic / international travel up to 25%, primarily for customer discovery, go-lives and escalations.

Remote (United States)

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
**About OpenLoop**
------------------

OpenLoop was co-founded by CEO, Dr. Jon Lensing, and COO, Christian Williams, with the vision to bring care anywhere. Our telehealth support solutions are thoughtfully designed to streamline and simplify go-to-market care delivery for companies offering meaningful virtual support to patients across an expansive array of specialties, in all 50 states.

### **About the Role**

Forward Deployed Engineering is how we build that platform with real clients instead of guessing. An FDE embeds with a client, works in the client's own codebase, and builds their integration against OpenLoop's production API. Whatever the client needs that the platform cannot do yet is filed as a platform gap and built once, centrally, so every client inherits it. The work product of an FDE is not the client's integration; it is the reusable asset that client forced into existence: a recipe others start from, an executable check behind every claim in our docs, a client manifest that makes the impact of any platform change computable, and the SDKs, agents and tooling that make the next deployment faster than the last.

You will write production code in two places, the client's system and ours. You will take an ask that is vague or over-promised and turn it into a scope you can defend. You will tell a client, and our own sales team, when something should not be committed to. And you will leave every deployment better instrumented than you found it, so the next client needs less of us than the last one did.

We are hiring for this role at the Senior, Staff and Senior Staff levels. Apply once; we will calibrate level during the process based on the scope you have carried, not on years alone. The section below describes what changes as scope grows.

### **What You'll Do**

* Build for clients, in their codebase, against our API. Embed with a client's engineering team and stand up their integration on OpenLoop's Partner API: their app, their data, their identity, their legacy systems. Own the outcome through go-live and the weeks after it. Never wire around the platform: where the API falls short, file the gap with the endpoint it stands in for, and leave a dated, time-boxed workaround at most.
* Build with AI in the loop, for clients and for us. Ship the systems that let a client build on us with AI in the loop: SDKs and reference implementations, a CLI and machine-readable docs a client can hand to their own coding agent, and agentic workflows on our API such as intake, routing, support and refill journeys, with human review by design, evaluations before launch and monitoring after.
* Run deployments on the agent roster, and make it better. Use and extend the agents that run our deployments: the tenant readiness gate, conformance checks against a live tenant, seeding checkers, docs-freshness and superseding drafts, gap filing, client communication drafts. Every agent output is a draft a human approves, and you are accountable for knowing when the agent is wrong.
* Turn one client's need into every client's capability. Contribute additive recipes and checks to the shared cookbook, keep client manifests current, and bring the evidence that moves a recurring workaround into the platform roadmap instead of into another workaround. The measure is how much less of us the next client needs.
* Turn ambiguity into a plan. Take a client ask that is vague, over-promised or self-contradictory and produce a phased, defensible scope, with a clear statement of what we are not doing and what the API does not do yet.
* Never undo prior work. Checks lock the claims we publish; manifests tell you who depends on what; edits are additive or explicitly superseding with a compatibility window. A change that would break a live client stops and becomes a proposal, not a merge.
* Hold the line, internally and externally. Be the credible technical voice with client engineering and with our own go-to-market team: what we cannot do, what we should not do, and what will not fit the timeline are three different answers, and all three are better delivered early.
* Raise the bar around you. Share what a deployment taught you, review other people's integration designs, and help write the playbook for a team that is being built now.

### **Who You Are**

* 5 to 15+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time delivering directly for external customers or partners, in their environments, not only internal roadmap work. We are filling roles across this range; depth of ownership matters more to us than the number.
* End-to-end ownership of complex, customer-facing technical delivery: you can name the deployments you ran, what went wrong, and what you did about it after launch.
* Strong integration engineering depth: API design and consumption, auth, webhooks versus polling, idempotency, rate limits, pagination, schema drift, reconciliation, and comfort across the stack from APIs to data to cloud infrastructure.
* You build with AI agents every day and can show how you verify what they produce, when you stop trusting them, and how you evaluate an LLM-based system before it reaches a customer.
* Experience handling sensitive data with a security-first mindset, treating compliance constraints as design inputs rather than follow-ups.
* Excellent communication with technical and non-technical audiences, including delivering unwelcome news to a customer early and keeping the relationship.
* Demonstrated judgment about scope: you can point to things you descoped, sequenced or declined, and explain why.
* Evidence of leverage beyond your own delivery: SDKs, tooling, checks, reference implementations or practices you built that made other people's work faster. The scale of that leverage is part of how we calibrate level.

**Preferred**

* Experience in healthcare or another regulated domain where a mistake has consequences beyond a rollback.
* Practical experience shipping LLM-based or agentic systems to production, including how you measured quality and what you did when the model was confidently wrong.
* Experience building developer platforms: SDKs, CLIs, API conventions, documentation that is tested rather than written.
* Familiarity with EHR, scheduling, pharmacy or payments integrations; FHIR is a plus.
* Experience working alongside sales or solutions teams in pre-sales technical conversations without becoming a blocker.
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

### **How You Work**

OpenLoop's values are prescriptive, and this role tests all of them:

Disciplined Intensity: effective under real deadline pressure, and you build systems instead of becoming the only person who can fix things.

Do No Harm: patient safety and data integrity come first, and you know when to slow down to do it right.

Step In, Stay In: your ownership travels to the outcome, not to the handoff.

Purposeful Speed: you ship fast without leaving behind something only you can maintain.

Clarity Over Comfort: you say the thing, explain the why, and invite disagreement.

Core collaboration hours are CST 8am to 5pm, with client-facing work occasionally requiring flexibility outside them. Remote within the United States; periodic travel to clients and to team working sessions.

**Our Benefits**
----------------

In addition, for salaried positions you would also be eligible for:

* Medical, Dental, and Vision plans
* Flexible Spending/Health Savings Accounts
* Flexible PTO
* 401(k) + Company Match
* Life Insurance, Pet insurance, and more

**Our Company**
---------------

We have a relatively flat organizational structure here at OpenLoop. Everyone is encouraged to bring ideas to the table and make things happen. This fits in well with our core values of Autonomy, Competence and Belonging, as we want everyone to feel empowered and supported to do their best work.

Sound like a good fit? We’d love to meet you.

title: FDE Security & Identity Engineer - USA
description:
**FDE Security & Identity Engineer**

This is a remote, client-facing consultant role with Inviso. In this position, you will support an external software development organization as part of Inviso’s delivery team, working closely with client product, engineering, security, and business stakeholders.

The Inviso Security & Identity Engineer is responsible for helping design, secure, and deliver the foundations of an enterprise AI platform used in mission-critical transportation and operational technology environments. This role focuses on threat modeling, tenant isolation, identity, authorization, secure delivery practices, and compliance-by-design.

You will work with client teams to make sure the platform is safe by construction, with security decisions built into the architecture rather than added after the fact. The ideal candidate is hands-on, pragmatic, collaborative, and able to explain complex security concepts clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

This is a 100% remote role, but may require some travel due to client needs.

**Experience & Skills Required**

* Experience designing and securing production software platforms, preferably in multi-tenant or regulated environments.
* Strong understanding of authentication, authorization, delegated access, token exchange, service identity, and least-privilege access patterns.
* Experience defining or contributing to platform threat models and applying them to architecture, engineering, and delivery decisions.
* Ability to design and review tenant isolation models across control plane, data plane, application, and infrastructure boundaries.
* Experience securing systems that execute untrusted content, code, tools, or agent actions.
* Familiarity with secure CI/CD practices including secrets management, scanning, policy enforcement, and secure release controls.
* Ability to support compliance-by-design practices including controls, evidence, data handling, and security documentation.
* Strong communication skills and ability to partner with engineers, product leaders, client stakeholders, and customer security teams.
* Pragmatic judgment with the ability to balance security, speed, reliability, and business value.
* Interest in responsible AI, secure AI systems, and controls for model, agent, and tool-based workflows.

**Desired Qualifications**

* Experience designing authentication and authorization for a multi-tenant SaaS or platform environment.

title: Agent Strategist
description:
Fragment is the AI platform that autonomously streamlines procurement workflows end to end. Within a few months of launch, we signed Fortune 500 companies. Within a year of founding, our customers, all $1B+ revenue enterprises, continue to grow in number and are actively championing us to their networks, and our marketing and CAC to get here has been $0.

We're hiring Agent Strategists to own the end-to-end deployment of Fragment's agents inside enterprise customers, from first workshop to live agents resolving work in production. You sit between the customer and our engineering and research teams. You learn their process cold, define the agents that automate it, get them live fast, and stay accountable for the outcomes after go-live.

**Company Highlights**

* **The Team:** Our CEO previously led and scaled three of Zoom's products past $300M in revenue, and our CTO is an ex-AI researcher who has spent his entire career in enterprise AI, leading engineering teams from seed through Series C. The broader team includes repeat VC-backed founders, Caltech PhDs, former quants, chess masters, Six Sigma Master Black Belts, and one very enthusiastic Bonsai grower.
* **Product:** We pride ourselves on our depth of our experience building agents, and on our continued diligence in leveraging the latest technology. We hold a high bar of excellence that starts with the founding team.
* **Hypergrowth:** 30x revenue growth in the first half of this year, with the majority of our pipeline coming from customer references.

**What We've Built**

Every large enterprise runs procurement software. Coupa, SAP Ariba, Jaggaer, GEP. These systems digitize the process, but they don't resolve exceptions. When a 3-way match fails, when a change order hits after goods receipt, when a duplicate invoice slips through across ERPs, those platforms route the problem to a human. The human investigates, makes a judgment call, and closes the loop. That's why organizations have large workforce to do work that is repetitive, rules-based, and high-volume, rather than the high-value strategic work.

Fragment replaces that repetitive non-value work with AI agents that actually resolve exceptions end to end. Not routing. Not flagging. Resolution. Our platform reasons across ERP systems, procurement documents, supplier data, custom databases, SaaS solutions, and tribal knowledge simultaneously. It doesn't require a rip-and-replace. It doesn't need months of integration work. It deploys on top of whatever systems a customer already runs and starts resolving exceptions autonomously.

In deployments with Fortune 500 customers, we've realized dramatic reductions in the amount of time a buyer and an AP analyst spend chasing exceptions every day. We are the only company that profits from procurement process exceptions going to zero.

**What You'll Do**

* **Customer Discovery & Definition.** Walk into customers across different industries, different ERPs, and different levels of process maturity, and get productive fast. Facilitate workshops with enterprise stakeholders to map their procurement and source-to-pay processes and identify the highest-value opportunities for autonomous agents. Design the agent definitions that automate that work, tailored to each customer's priorities, data, and systems, and design the future-state workflows for how humans and AI agents share the work. Help customers see what's possible when AI agents handle the work their BPOs and shared services teams do today.
* **Customer Facing Delivery Work.** Be hands-on in launching and configuring customer deployments. Connect Fragment to customer systems of record (ERP and adjacent procurement systems) so agents operate cleanly against live data. Own deployment readiness: make sure the process logic, exception handling, and workflow configuration are dialed in before we go live. Deploy at high velocity, driving rapid time-to-value and measurable ROI from day one, and run each engagement with the project management and iterative delivery that keep momentum and transparency across customer and Fragment teams. Build the playbooks, process documentation, and implementation frameworks that let us scale delivery beyond your individual involvement.
* **Product Work.** Partner with our engineering team to continuously refine and expand the platform's procurement capabilities. Bring real-world process knowledge into the product loop, surfacing edge cases, validating automation logic, and ensuring that what we ship holds up against the complexity of actual enterprise procurement environments. Guide the UX from a practitioner's perspective so the product feels intuitive to the teams who use it daily. Bring your field learnings back to our research and product teams so the agents and the roadmap keep getting better.
* **Strategic Work.** Help shape Fragment's point of view on what lean procure-to-pay and source-to-pay processes should look like when AI agents are in the loop. Not incremental optimization of the status quo. A fundamental rethinking of how these processes are designed when autonomous resolution is the default, not the exception. Contribute to thought leadership and strengthen our go-to-market messaging with operational depth.
* **Advisor & Expansion.** Stay accountable for business KPIs and outcomes after go-live, not just launch. Serve as a trusted advisor on how customers get the most out of agentic AI across their operations, and unlock new opportunities to expand where agents are deployed. Bring the autonomous future to life for customers, helping them see not just what agents do today but how autonomous operations reshape their procurement strategy tomorrow.

This is a startup. You'll go deep on source-to-pay processes, but you'll also be pulled into whatever needs to get done. If you need a clearly scoped job description to be comfortable, this isn't the right fit.

**Who You Are**

This role rewards slope over résumé. The best Agent Strategists learn ridiculously fast, think in systems, and are as comfortable with a VP of Procurement as they are whiteboarding logic with engineers. Some arrive with deep procurement and deployment experience. Others arrive with raw horsepower and pick up the domain fast. Both work.

You might come from one of these paths:

* **The practitioner-consultant.** You did real procurement or operations work inside a large enterprise, then moved into consulting and built breadth across industries, ERPs, and transformation methodologies. You have the intuition from having lived it and the structure from consulting.
* **The forward-deployed or solutions engineer.** You've deployed complex software into enterprises at a high-growth company, sat in front of customers, owned outcomes, and seen forward-deployed work done well. You may not know procurement yet, but you know how to land a hard product in a messy environment.
* **The high-slope generalist.** You come from top-tier consulting or a top MBA program, you ramp on new domains faster than anyone around you, and you want real ownership instead of slideware. You'll go deep on procurement quickly, because that's how you operate with everything.

Whatever the path, we're looking for 7+ years of relevant experience.

Regardless of background, you are someone who:

* Learns ridiculously fast. You can walk into a company you've never seen, sit with their team, and produce a clear process map with decision trees, exception paths, and system touchpoints within days.
* Thinks in systems, not tickets, and context-switches across industries and ERP environments without a long ramp. Our customers span electronics manufacturing, energy, automotive, food and beverage, and more, running SAP, Oracle, Coupa, Ariba, and homegrown systems, sometimes all at once.
* Translates between practitioners and engineers. You can take a procurement team's messy description of how they handle exceptions and turn it into structured logic an engineering team can build against.
* Combines technical literacy (SQL comfort, ERP schemas, a practical understanding of agentic workflows) with strong executive communication.
* Is comfortable on-site with clients, thrives in a high-velocity environment, and measures success by customer adoption and expansion.
* Takes ownership under pressure, with an instinct to run toward the fire.

**Nice to Have**

* Experience deploying or configuring enterprise AI or SaaS platforms as an FDE, applied engineer, or deployment specialist
* Familiarity with enterprise data pipelines and integrations with existing systems
* Exposure to the agentic AI ecosystem, LLMs, or automation platforms
* Prior experience at a startup or in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment

**Interested?** Reach out even if you’re not sure you’re a perfect fit.

Compensation Range: $250K - $400K

**Title:** Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)  
**Reports to:** Director of Professional Services  
**Department:** Professional Services  
**Location:** Remote within the United States  
**Status:** Exempt

  
  

**About Atlas Technica**
------------------------

Atlas Technica's mission is to shoulder IT management, user support, and cybersecurity for our clients, who are hedge funds and other investment firms. Founded in 2016, we have grown year over year through our uncompromising focus on service.

We value ownership, execution, growth, intelligence, and camaraderie. We are looking for people who share our core values, thrive in a collaborative environment, and put the customer first. Atlas Technica offers competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and valuable perks to our global team. We are committed to maintaining a professional yet friendly environment that supports the continued growth and career development of our team members. Join Atlas Technica and grow with us!

**Position Overview**
---------------------

As a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) at Atlas Technica, you will serve as a senior, client-facing technical advisor working directly with prospective and existing clients to evaluate their technology environments and identify opportunities for improvement. This role is focused on conducting technical discovery, operational assessments, and gap analyses to uncover risks, inefficiencies, and modernization opportunities across client environments.

The FDE works closely with clients to understand how their technology supports their business and where improvements can be made across infrastructure, security, cloud, and IT operations. Based on these findings, the FDE develops clear recommendations and strategic technology roadmaps designed to improve reliability, security, scalability, and operational maturity.

This role also partners closely with Atlas sales, solutions, engineering, and delivery teams to translate assessment findings into practical implementation strategies and well-defined engagements. The Forward Deployed Engineer acts as a trusted technical advisor to clients while helping Atlas identify opportunities where our services can provide meaningful and lasting value.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Conduct technical discovery sessions with prospective and existing clients to understand their infrastructure, security posture, operational processes, and business requirements.
* Perform comprehensive technology assessments and gap analyses across infrastructure, cloud platforms, identity systems, security controls, and IT operations.
* Evaluate client environments that may include Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, endpoint management, networking, backup and recovery, identity systems, and cybersecurity tooling.
* Identify operational inefficiencies, security risks, architectural limitations, and opportunities for modernization.
* Develop actionable recommendations and strategic technology roadmaps aligned with client needs and industry best practices.
* Translate complex technical findings into clear summaries and recommendations for both technical teams and business stakeholders.
* Partner with sales and solutions teams during early-stage client engagements to help shape potential project scopes and solution strategies.
* Collaborate with Professional Services and engineering teams to ensure proposed solutions align with Atlas delivery capabilities and technical standards.
* Participate in remote and onsite client engagements to conduct in-depth discovery and assessments when required.
* Document assessment findings, recommendations, risks, and proposed improvement initiatives in a clear and structured manner.
* Serve as a trusted technical advisor during client discovery sessions, strategic discussions, and early-stage engagements.
* Identify opportunities for Atlas Technica services to improve clients' operational maturity, security posture, and overall technology performance.
* Stay informed on emerging technologies, cybersecurity trends, and industry best practices relevant to financial services organizations.
* Provide feedback to internal teams on recurring client challenges and market needs to help strengthen Atlas service offerings, methodologies, and internal playbooks.

**Requirements**
----------------

* 7+ years of experience in IT infrastructure, cloud engineering, systems engineering, solution architecture, or a related technical discipline.
* Strong experience across Microsoft 365, Azure, AWS, networking, identity platforms, endpoint management, and modern security technologies.
* Experience conducting technical assessments, infrastructure reviews, security evaluations, or operational maturity assessments.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex technology environments and identify practical improvement opportunities.
* Excellent communication skills, including the ability to translate complex technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations.
* Experience supporting technical discovery, pre-sales engagements, or client advisory work within a consulting, MSP, or professional services environment.
* Strong documentation and presentation skills, including experience producing technical assessment reports, executive summaries, and roadmap recommendations.
* Deep understanding of modern IT architecture, including hybrid cloud environments, identity security, endpoint management, networking, and security controls.
* Ability to collaborate effectively with sales, solutions, delivery, engineering, and leadership teams.
* Ability and willingness to travel for onsite client engagements as needed.

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience working with financial services organizations, hedge funds, investment firms, or other regulated environments.
* Experience working within a Managed Service Provider (MSP), consulting firm, or professional services organization.
* Relevant certifications such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert, AWS Certified Solutions Architect, CISSP, or similar.
* Experience designing or evaluating cloud migrations, security transformations, infrastructure modernization initiatives, or technology operating models.
* Familiarity with compliance frameworks and operational requirements relevant to financial services organizations.
* Experience with enterprise platforms and technologies such as Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Intune, Azure security services, or similar tools.

Atlas Technica is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, protected veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Sr. Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
**About Re:Build**
------------------

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.

We operate an advanced, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.

The way we operate is as important as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and contribute to the communities where we operate. *(link to* *The Re:Build Way principles**)*

  

**Who we are looking for**
--------------------------

Digital innovation is central to Re:Build Manufacturing's mission and essential for scaling as a world-class industrial company. The Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) in the Digital Innovation Group (DIG) works directly at Re:Build sites alongside collaborators. They quickly prototype and deliver full-stack digital solutions that address real business challenges and create measurable impact. The FDE uses technical skills, AI knowledge, and awareness of industry developments to provide these solutions. They lead client workshops, develop solution strategies, manage critical technical issues, and cultivate positive relationships with site teams. The FDE also ensures risk management by aligning solutions with DIG's security protocols, data standards, and AI governance guidelines while following coding practices. This role suits experienced engineers who combine strong technical insight, customer focus, product awareness, and who excel in responsibility and ownership.

**What you get to do**
----------------------

* Collaborate directly with team members to understand business processes, difficulties, and success criteria; and proactively uncover new opportunities to implement digital solutions.
* Own the full lifecycle of prototypes and production solutions, from discovery and prioritization through build, deployment, and post-launch iteration.
* Build prototype solutions to validate approaches and accelerate discovery.
* Use knowledge in AI and machine learning to recommend approaches where AI can generate measurable business impact for interested parties.
* Bring external innovation to internal problems.
* Identify and resolve bugs in prototypes while optimizing code for performance and scalability.
* Provide technical mentorship and support throughout implementation, including resolving issues, optimization, and adoption support.
* Contribute to software build and architecture, ensuring scalability and reliability in line with team goals.
* Ensure adherence to guidelines and coding standards through code reviews.
* Develop and maintain technical documentation, implementation playbooks, and reusable assets to accelerate future deployments.
* Risk, security, and compliance leadership: Guarantee that implementations meet DIG's security protocols, data management criteria, and AI governance standards.
* Travel up to 50% of the time to portfolio locations, mainly stationed at a particular site to speed up solution implementation (domestic US travel only).
* Other responsibilities as assigned.

**What you bring to the Team**
------------------------------

* 3+ years of software engineering, solutions platform delivery or technical implementation experience, ideally in customer-facing contexts.
* Experienced in programming languages such as Python or similar, with a strong understanding of APIs and systems integration.
* Ability to rapidly understand unfamiliar technical ecosystems and workflows and build integration paths.
* Excellent communication skills. Confident translating for both technical and non-technical collaborators.
* High ownership approach with comfort operating independently, navigating ambiguity.
* Demonstrated experience working with enterprise customers; particularly in manufacturing, quality, engineering services, or supply chain operations.
* Experience with LLMs, generative AI pipelines and agent-style automation frameworks (agent workflows, tool orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation).
* Prior consulting, technical solution engineering or internal tools engineering experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex customer deployments involving cloud infrastructure, identity/SSO, data access, and integration with enterprise systems.
* Proven ability to establish standards and operating rhythm (playbooks, quality gates, blocking issue models, delivery targets) across distributed teams.
* Executive-level collaborator management: able to communicate with senior collaborators; adept at navigating ambiguity and driving decisions.
* Ability to travel up to 50% of the time, with extended periods embedded at specific collaborator sites.

**Preferred Qualifications:**
-----------------------------

* Solid engineering foundation. Desired areas of study include, though are not restricted to, Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, and Machine Learning.
* Familiarity with enterprise ecosystems such as Snowflake, Atlassian suite of tools, and common integration approaches.
* Background in regulated industries and governance-heavy environments (auditability, privacy, retention).
* Ability to operate autonomously, thrive under ambiguity, and represent DIG at the highest level in customer environments.
* Experience partnering with product teams on platformization (turning custom work into reusable product capabilities).
* Prior enterprise delivery leadership experience driving multi-workstream execution, program governance, and executive steering across complex collaborator environments.

**Export Control Requirement:** Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

The base salary range for this position is $120,223.00 – $180,334.00 per year. This range represents the Company's good faith estimate of the base compensation for this role at the time of posting. Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to relevant experience, skills, qualifications, internal equity, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for annual incentive compensation and/or long-term incentives, subject to Company plans. The Company offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, retirement, paid time off, and other benefits.

**The BIG payoff**

We are a company who is going to make a difference in the industries and the communities in which we choose to operate.

Every employee of Re:Build will share ownership in the company and will share in the financial rewards of the success we achieve together, at all levels of the company!

**We want to work with people that reflect the communities in which we operate**

Re:Build Manufacturing is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, marital status, parental status, cultural background, organizational level, work styles, tenure and life experiences. Or for any other reason.

Re:Build is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at accommodations.ta@ReBuildmanufacturing.com or you may call us at 617.909.6275.
